answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the velvet ordering is published with the horizon batch, the jade audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 19% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 24 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
